reason: The cited lines define a read-only Sentry issue search requiring `event:read` and format returned Sentry issue data such as issue IDs, titles, status, user/event counts, assignee, timestamps, and culprit, so they support that the tool returns non-public SaaS issue data. Those returned issue fields, especially titles/culprits derived from captured events, can contain attacker-controlled content. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, nor do they show sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; they only build output links/text for the user.
